request: Short FPS drops (to ~50) when entering a room, breaking objects or seeing new areas; record 15 s with F8 and analyze
tooling: F8 records 15 s (was 10) without needing the F9 panel; an on-screen notice shows recording progress and the save.

stack_profile v3: each sampling sweep is stamped ('s <ms>'); 'c <ms> presents dvd_bytes texture_upload_bytes pipelines_created' lines record every counter change. New APIs: aurora_get_present_count, aurora_get_texture_upload_bytes_total, PrimeDvdBytesReadTotal.
Analyzer (scratchpad hitch.py): slow presents, counters per slow frame, per-thread inclusive functions inside vs outside hitch windows.

findings.texture_burst: One ~103 ms frame in each recording with ~50 MB of new texture data uploaded (room textures). GX thread in that frame: 76% creating textures; arb_mip_check 31% (single-threaded downscale+compare of every mip chain), CMPR decode 19% (already parallel), Dawn/D3D12 texture creation and upload ~28%.
findings.disc_streaming: ~700 ms of 25-55 ms frames while the game streams: 153 serialized disc reads, 5.6 MB. The IPC reply delay model (600 us + 32 MiB/s per read, Dolphin hardware figures) summed 259 ms; the game thread was idle 20% of that window waiting for replies (vs <4% elsewhere). nod decrypt/read on the game thread ~10%.

changes: aurora lib/gfx/texture_convert.cpp: downscale() and avg_diff() split rows across the decode pool. avg_diff accumulates integer squared differences (exact, order independent), so hasArbitraryMips is bit-identical to the serial version.

Option 'Lectura de disco rapida' ([prime] fast_disc_reads, WII_COMPILED_PRIME_FAST_DISC_READS, F1 > Rendimiento, live): disc read replies use a fixed 200 us delay instead of the drive model. Default on. A nonzero delay is kept so a reply never completes on the submission stack (FMOD case documented in memory.cpp).
not_done: Texture creation/upload in Dawn (~28% of the burst frame) and CMPR->RGBA8 expansion (8x data) remain; uploading CMPR as BC1 would cut both but changes decoding details and needs a fidelity review.
Disc reads still run synchronously on the game thread (nod decrypt); moving them to a worker during the reply delay is deferred.

second_recording_2026-10-24.profile: stack_profile_20261024_000447.txt (20 s, morph ball and a short walk)
findings: 137-222 ms frames coincide with new pipelines (+1..+13): the game thread waited 79% in aurora_wait_for_frame_worker while the GX thread idled, i.e. the frame worker blocked on first-use shader compiles. Startup prewarm had loaded 4759 pipelines (all Dawn blob hits); the cache held 5144 after the session, so these are first-use only and are prewarmed on the next start.
38-43 ms frames with ~2 MB disc reads per frame: nod sector-group decryption on the game thread (~15%); the disc was opened with preloader_threads = 0.
105-111 ms frames with 2-3 MB new textures: texture creation on the GX thread plus frame-worker waits.
changes: F8 also samples the frame worker and presenter threads (aurora_get_render_thread_ids); profiles list 'threads game gx frame_worker presenter'.
nod disc opened with preloader_threads = 2 so following sector groups are decrypted ahead of the read position.
